slot.brief: A block released from rest on a smooth track slides down and compresses a spring; ask for maximum compression using energy conservation (no figure).

stem: A block of mass 1 kg is released from rest at a height 2 m on a smooth curved track. It slides down onto a horizontal smooth surface and compresses a spring of force constant 160 N/m. Taking g = 10 m/s^2, the maximum compression produced in the spring is

verdicts.working: By energy conservation, mgh = ½kx². Thus 1×10×2 = ½×160×x², giving x = 0.50 m.

working:
mgh = (1/2) k x_max^2. 1 x 10 x 2 = 0.5 x 160 x x^2. 20 = 80 x^2, so x^2 = 0.25 and x_max = 0.50 m.

Independent check: By energy conservation, mgh = ½kx². Thus 1×10×2 = ½×160×x², giving x = 0.50 m.
solution:
By conservation of mechanical energy, the block’s gravitational potential energy is stored in the spring at maximum compression:
$$mgh=\frac12kx^2$$
$$1\times10\times2=\frac12(160)x^2\quad\Rightarrow\quad x=0.50\,\text{m}$$
